Definition: another (active) form for G2516; to seat down, i.e. set (figuratively, appoint); intransitively, to sit (down); figuratively, to settle (hover, dwell):--continue, set, sit (down), tarry.
BiblicalUsage: Kathizo means to sit down, to take a seat, and so to settle and rule. Matthew 25:31 says when the Son of man shall come in his glory, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory. Luke 14:28 asks which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost. 1 Corinthians 6:4 tells the church to set the least esteemed to judge, and Revelation 20:4 says I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sitting is the posture of authority: Christ sits to judge, and his people sit with him. I hold that counting the cost is sitting down first, not rushing to build. My position is that the throne belongs to the Son of man, and I want to be found on his side when he sits.
